parameters.toolDescription:
Get the full claim text of one published patent document from EPO Open Patent Services.

COVERAGE IS LIMITED. OPS full-text serves EP and WO documents reliably, plus some national collections. It does NOT serve US full text — a US number returns CLIENT.InvalidCountryCode. For US claims use a USPTO tool instead. A document that was withdrawn or refused before grant may also have no full text and returns SERVER.EntityNotFound; that is correct behaviour, not an error in the request.

Use for claim construction, comparing an EP family member against its counterpart, or reading the claims of EP/WO prior art. Granted EP patents (B1) return the claims as granted, in DE, EN and FR.

parameters.toolDescription:
Get the full description (specification) text of one published patent document from EPO Open Patent Services.

COVERAGE IS LIMITED, exactly as for EPO Claims: EP and WO are served, US is NOT (a US number returns CLIENT.InvalidCountryCode — use a USPTO tool for US specifications). Documents withdrawn before grant may return SERVER.EntityNotFound.

Responses are very large and count against the EPO data quota — prefer EPO Biblio or EPO Claims unless the specification text itself is genuinely needed.

parameters.toolDescription:
Get the INPADOC legal-status event timeline for one publication — grant, lapse, opposition filed or withdrawn, transfer of rights, SPC extension, fee payment, withdrawal. Use to determine whether a patent is currently in force in a given state, when it lapsed, or whether it has been opposed. For EP cases the EPO Register tool gives a richer procedural history.

Events such as FIRST EXAMINATION REPORT DESPATCHED or APPLICATION WITHDRAWN tell you a document exists but not what it says — the underlying papers are only in EPO file inspection, which no API exposes. When the user asks to read one, give them:

https://register.epo.org/application?number=EP{APPNUM}&lng=en&tab=doclist

where {APPNUM} is the EP application number, available in this response as ops:L003EP (Document Number) for EP events, e.g. 14749020 gives https://register.epo.org/application?number=EP14749020&lng=en&tab=doclist.

A trailing kind code such as A1 or B1 is stripped automatically.", "string").toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g, "").replace(/[A-Z][0-9]{0,2}$/, "") }}

parameters.toolDescription:
Get the European Patent Register record for one EP or PCT publication — bibliographic data, procedural events, and procedural steps (entry into regional phase, examination communications, amendments, renewal fee payments, oppositions, transfers). EP and PCT only.

IMPORTANT — this records THAT an event occurred, not the text of the document. EPO file inspection documents (Art. 94(3) communications, applicant replies, minutes, opposition briefs) are NOT available through any API. When the user needs to read one, ALWAYS give them this deep link:

https://register.epo.org/application?number=EP{APPNUM}&lng=en&tab=doclist

where {APPNUM} is the EP application number without the EP prefix or check digit — take it from reg:application-reference > reg:doc-number in this response (e.g. 14749020 gives https://register.epo.org/application?number=EP14749020&lng=en&tab=doclist). The Register is keyed on the APPLICATION number; a publication number will not work. Present the link explicitly rather than only mentioning that file inspection exists.

If the user wants those, get the EP application number from EPO Register or EPO Biblio and give them this deep link:

https://register.epo.org/application?number=EP{APPNUM}&lng=en&tab=doclist

(e.g. application 14749020 gives https://register.epo.org/application?number=EP14749020&lng=en&tab=doclist). The Register is keyed on the APPLICATION number, not the publication number.

parameters.description:
Download a range of pages from an EPO published document and OCR them to markdown, returned in page order with a '## Page N' heading before each.

You MUST first call EPO List Documents to obtain a documentLink AND the section start-pages; this tool cannot find a document by description. EPO List Documents reports where each section begins (e.g. CLAIMS at page 44, SEARCH_REPORT at page 56), so target the section you actually want rather than reading from page 1.

EPO's API serves only one page per request, so this tool loops internally — a 10-page range means 10 OPS calls and 10 OCR pages. The range is capped at 20 pages per call. Keep ranges tight: each page counts against the EPO data quota and is billed as OCR. For a single page, set pageStart only and leave pageEnd at its default.
